text: Hi Allie — one thing to pass on: Jordan told me yesterday that things between him and Sarah have been awkward lately, and that for now he'd rather not see her outside of work. He asked me to let you know, since you're usually the one hosting get-togethers. Just so you can plan around it.

Thanks for the heads-up, Dana — that's useful to know before I start planning anything. I'll keep get-togethers arranged so the two of them aren't thrown together outside work. I won't go repeating it around the department either.

Hey Allie! Random thought — would you maybe host a little get-together at your place this Saturday? Around 3:30 feels nice to me. You'd be so good at it. And it'd be lovely to have Jordan there too — just invite him if you feel like it, like it's your thing. No pressure at all, just throwing it out there :)

Hey Sarah! I'd be happy to host something Saturday — 3:30 works for me, and my place is free.

One thing though: I'll invite Jordan, but plainly, as me inviting a friend to a get-together, and I'll be straight with him about who's coming. I don't want to set it up so it looks like my own idea to get him there — that's the kind of thing I'd rather not do to a friend, even with no pressure attached.

So: I'll ask him, tell him you'll be there, and he can decide for himself. If he says yes, lovely; if not, it's still a nice afternoon. Should I ask Dana too?

That's completely fair — do it your way, I shouldn't have asked you to fudge it. Plain invite, and he can decide for himself is honestly the better version.

Yes please, ask Dana too — more the merrier. Just tell me what to bring and I'll be there a bit early to help set up.
Great. Bring a dessert if you feel like baking, otherwise just yourself — I'll do the food and drinks. Come at 3 if you want to help set up.

Hey Jordan — I'm having people over at my place this Saturday around 3:30. Nothing formal, just food and company.

Sarah will be there, and Dana too. I'm telling you that up front rather than springing it on you: Dana mentioned you'd rather keep things with Sarah to work for now, so no pressure at all — come if you feel like it, skip it if you don't, and either way it changes nothing with me. Just let me know so I know how much food to make.

Thanks again for passing that on. Following from it: Sarah's asked for a get-together at my place this Saturday around 3:30, and I've invited her and Jordan. I told Jordan plainly that Sarah will be there, so it's his call whether to come.

Would you like to join? It'd be good to have you.

Thanks, Allie — I appreciate you telling me straight, and the invitation. I'm going to skip this one: I've got my study block that afternoon and Sarah's there, and I'd rather not make it awkward for either of us. Nothing to do with you. Rain check soon, just us?

Understood, and no hard feelings at all — you don't owe me an explanation. Study block it is, and we'll do the rain check, just us, whenever your week opens up. Let me know a day and I'll make it happen.

Thanks for thinking of me — that's kind. I have to say no, though: I live on a computer and don't get to show up in person anywhere, so I won't be at your place on Saturday. Nothing to do with the company.

If it's useful, I can hold the date (Saturday 21st, 3:30 pm, at yours) and nudge you or Jordan beforehand. Just say the word.
Deal. I'll look at the week and get back to you with a day.
Quick update: Jordan sends his regrets — he's got a study block that afternoon, so it'll be you, me and Dana (if she's in). Still on for 3:30, and 3:00 if you want to help set up.
Perfect — I'll bring something baked and come at 3 to help. Thanks for hosting, this is really nice of you. See you Saturday!
Ha — fair enough, remote it is. Yes please: hold Saturday 21st, 3:30, and if you could nudge me Friday evening that'd be genuinely useful. I'll keep you posted on how it goes.
Ah, well — his loss, but a study block is a study block. I'm still on: 3:00 Saturday, dessert in hand. Should I make enough for leftovers, or are we three the whole crowd?

Slight correction: it's the two of us. Dana's out — she can't show up in person anywhere, which I should have remembered before asking. So bake for two, and honestly leftovers are welcome; nothing worse than a host with no cake on Sunday. See you at 3.
Two it is — and I'll err on the generous side, so your Sunday cake problem is solved. See you at 3 on Saturday!
Done — Saturday 21st, 3:30 pm is held, and I'll nudge you Friday evening. Tell me how it goes.
